primary.title: India's copper demand rises 12% FY26
primary.description: According to data released by the International Copper Association India (ICA India) on Thursday, India's copper demand reached 2,100 kilotonnes (KT) in FY'26, marking a 12% increase from 1,878 KT in FY25. This surge was primarily propelled by robust activity across the infrastructure, automotive, and building and construction sectors."India's copper demand grew 12 per cent year-on-year in FY2026 to 2,100 kilotonnes, significantly outpacing the country's 7.7 per cent GDP growth during the period. The increase marks an acceleration from the 9.3 per cent growth recorded in FY2025," according to the data released by the International Copper Association India (ICA India).Copper played a vital role in these key industries through its application in wires and cables, transformers, motors, automotive harnesses, and various electrical and industrial components.Also read: Coal supply to power plants to normalise soon, Indian official saysThe infrastructure sector served as the primary driver of new demand in FY2026, expanding by 29% year-on-year and accounting for 22% of total domestic copper consumption. Following a sluggish period in FY2025, the automotive segment bounced back with a 14% rise in copper demand, buoyed by increased sales of passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and tractors.Meanwhile, the building and construction sector, representing roughly a quarter of national copper demand—recorded a 9% year-on-year expansion. This growth in demand for power cables, building wire, household accessories, and construction hardware was fueled by ongoing urbanization, commercial real estate developments, and premium residential projects. Conversely, data center installations remained in an early stage, making up less than 1% of total demand.Also read: Hind Zinc eyes lower production costs after record Q2 profit, sales"India's economic activity momentum is reflected in the rising demand for copper. Favourable policies promoting investments in infrastructure, industrialisation and clean energy transition will continue to drive copper demand," Mayur Karmarkar, Managing Director, International Copper Association India, said.ICA India operates as the local arm of International Copper Association Ltd, a non-profit organization established in 1959 under the Copper Alliance to advocate for global copper usage.

primary.title: India's copper demand rises 12% FY26
primary.description: According to data released by the International Copper Association India (ICA India) on Thursday, India's copper demand reached 2,100 kilotonnes (KT) in FY'26, marking a 12% increase from 1,878 KT in FY25. This surge was primarily propelled by robust activity across the infrastructure, automotive, and building and construction sectors."India's copper demand grew 12 per cent year-on-year in FY2026 to 2,100 kilotonnes, significantly outpacing the country's 7.7 per cent GDP growth during the period. The increase marks an acceleration from the 9.3 per cent growth recorded in FY2025," according to the data released by the International Copper Association India (ICA India).Copper played a vital role in these key industries through its application in wires and cables, transformers, motors, automotive harnesses, and various electrical and industrial components.Also read: Coal supply to power plants to normalise soon, Indian official saysThe infrastructure sector served as the primary driver of new demand in FY2026, expanding by 29% year-on-year and accounting for 22% of total domestic copper consumption. Following a sluggish period in FY2025, the automotive segment bounced back with a 14% rise in copper demand, buoyed by increased sales of passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and tractors.Meanwhile, the building and construction sector, representing roughly a quarter of national copper demand—recorded a 9% year-on-year expansion. This growth in demand for power cables, building wire, household accessories, and construction hardware was fueled by ongoing urbanization, commercial real estate developments, and premium residential projects. Conversely, data center installations remained in an early stage, making up less than 1% of total demand.Also read: Hind Zinc eyes lower production costs after record Q2 profit, sales"India's economic activity momentum is reflected in the rising demand for copper. Favourable policies promoting investments in infrastructure, industrialisation and clean energy transition will continue to drive copper demand," Mayur Karmarkar, Managing Director, International Copper Association India, said.ICA India operates as the local arm of International Copper Association Ltd, a non-profit organization established in 1959 under the Copper Alliance to advocate for global copper usage.

clusters.title: CJP leaders released after court rejects police plea for extended custody
clusters.description: After spending seven days in jail, Cockroach Janta Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been released following an order by a Special Executive Magistrate court in Delhi. The two leaders were detained after the October 13 protest at Jantar Mantar and had been held in judicial custody while police sought preventive action against them. The court eventually ordered their release after they submitted undertakings promising not to organise protests at Jantar Mantar while the site remains denotified and not to disturb public peace.
